diagnosis: HBV calibrated on 1971-10 to 1997-12 daily discharge (Lune at Killington), using a global DDS search (3000 runs) followed by a Nelder-Mead polish (600 runs). Calibration NSE is 0.857, KGE 0.89, r 0.93 and PBIAS -7.4% (the model underestimates total flow slightly). The catchment is wet and flashy, with thin soils and mostly impermeable rocks. The calibrated parameters fit that: a small FC (about 68 mm), high BETA (7.8), LP at its upper bound of 1, fast upper-zone responses (K0 0.31, K1 0.33), quick baseflow (K2 0.096) and short routing (MAXBAS 1.7). Snow plays a minor role (about 2% of precipitation falls as snow). The snow parameters are therefore poorly identified. CWH sits at its lower bound, but this has little effect. Likely weaknesses: peak flows are underestimated (simulated maximum 60 mm/d vs 92 mm/d observed), there is some volume deficit, and recessions and low flows in dry summers are uncertain. The objective stopped improving, so I am fairly confident in the main soil and response parameters. I expect the NSE in the independent period to be roughly 0.80–0.85. I did not run a split-sample validation test.
